summary:
Kisan Sahayak is an accessible, multilingual web application empowering smallholder farmers with real-time NASA Earth observation data, AI soil diagnostics, and direct rural market tools. By converting complex satellite telemetry (soil moisture, vegetation vitality, and surface temperature) into simple daily farming advice across 12+ Indian languages, Kisan Sahayak bridges orbital space technology with grassroots agriculture

Smallholder farmers suffer from unpredictable weather, soil degradation, water scarcity, and opaque market pricing. While NASA collects vital Earth observation data daily, it rarely reaches rural communities in actionable formats. Kisan Sahayak solves this by:

1. Democratizing NASA Satellite Telemetry: Translating NASA SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS (NDVI crop health), and VIIRS (surface temperature) data into an interactive field map with plain-language sowing and irrigation alerts.

2. Preventing Soil Degradation: Providing a multi-season crop rotation advisor (Rabi, Kharif, Zaid) tailored to live moisture levels to naturally restore soil nitrogen and organic carbon.

3. End-to-End Rural Support: Integrating an AI Soil & Leaf Photo Analyzer, Live APMC Mandi Prices, Government Policy Directory, Transport/Labour Booking, and KCC Loan tools into a lightweight interface optimized for basic mobile devices
details:
Kisan Sahayak is a satellite-powered smart farming and crop rotation web application built specifically for smallholder farmers. It integrates live Earth observation data from NASA POWER, SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS (vegetation health/NDVI), and VIIRS (surface temperature) APIs to provide real-time field telemetry and automated multi-season crop rotation advice.

Key features include an interactive 4-quadrant satellite map with a multi-spectral reflectance HUD, an AI-powered soil and leaf photo analyzer, live APMC Mandi price tracking, verified agricultural inputs marketplace, transport and labour hiring, and KCC loan application support. Developed using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, and HTML5 Canvas, the project empowers farmers across 12+ Indian languages with actionable, localized rural intelligence.
